app.appearance-settings.font.description.message: The typeface the app is set in. A letter the chosen font does not have is drawn in Inter.

app.appearance-settings.hide-nametag.des.message: Hide your username above the player preview on the Skin selector page.

app.appearance-settings.minimize-launche.message: Minimize Modrinth App when Minecraft starts.

app.appearance-settings.show-play-time.d.message: Show how long you've played each instance.

app.appearance-settings.skip-non-essenti.message: Skip confirmations for low-risk actions such as duplicate installs, normal content deletion, bulk updates, unlinking, and repairs. Warnings for dangerous actions are always shown.

app.appearance-settings.toggle-sidebar.d.message: Hide the right sidebar by default and add a button to show or hide it.

app.behavior-settings.hidden-instances.e.message: You haven't hidden any instances yet.

app.behavior-settings.refocus-on-game-cl.message: Bring Modrinth App to the foreground when Minecraft exits.

app.browse.server-instance-content-warni.message: Adding content may prevent you from joining this server. Any content you add will be removed when the managed server content is updated.

app.changelog.noctrinth-note.message: The full Noctrinth changelog is also available online.

app.collection.create.visibility-note.message: Your new collection will be created as a public collection with {count, plural, =0 {no projects} one {# project} other {# projects}}.

app.collection.delete-modal.description.message: This will permanently delete this collection. This action cannot be undone.

app.collection.delete-modal.title.message: Are you sure you want to delete this collection?

app.collection.save-button.empty.message: You don't have any collections yet.

app.collection.save-button.sign-in.message: Sign in to Modrinth to save projects.

app.content-install.curseforge.missing-d.message: These have no version for this instance and need to be added another way: {names}
Installed without some of its dependencies

app.content-install.no-compatible-versio.message: No available versions match {compatibilityLabel}. Select a version to install anyway. Dependencies will not be installed automatically.

app.content.sync-data-packs-disabled.message: Turn on data pack syncing in app settings first.

app.content.sync-packs-override.message: Turn off the pack syncing override in this instance’s settings first.

app.content.sync-resource-packs-disabled.message: Turn on resource pack syncing in app settings first.

app.crash-modal.nothing-found.message: The launcher did not recognise the cause. The log has the details, and can be shared from there.

app.crash.header-count.message: {count, plural, one {The launcher found a likely cause} other {The launcher found # likely causes}}

app.crash.memory-hint.message: It had {current} GB for {mods} mods. {gb} GB is what a pack this size usually needs, and this computer has it to spare.

app.crash.rule.broken-mod-file.fix.message: It is not a readable archive — a download that was cut off. Disable it and download it again.

app.crash.rule.chunk-unreadable.fix.message: Back the world up before doing anything else. A single damaged region file can be deleted and regenerated, losing only what was built there.

app.crash.rule.chunk-unreadable.title.message: Part of the world could not be read (chunk {chunk})

app.crash.rule.config-file-empty.fix.message: The game went down while saving it. Delete it and the mod will write it again with defaults.

app.crash.rule.config-truncated.fix.message: The game went down while saving it. Delete the file named in the line below and it will be written again with defaults.

app.crash.rule.config-truncated.title.message: A settings file is empty or cut short

app.crash.rule.config-unreadable.fix.message: Delete that file and start the game again — the mod will write a fresh one with its defaults.

app.crash.rule.connector-fabric-mod.fix.message: On NeoForge, install the mod's own NeoForge build where there is one — Sodium and Iris both have official ones, and they do not go through Connector. On Forge 1.20.1 and older the equivalents are Embeddium and Oculus.

app.crash.rule.connector-fabric-mod.titl.message: Sinytra Connector could not carry a Fabric mod ({exception})

app.crash.rule.corrupted-archive.fix.message: Repair the instance so the launcher fetches it again. A download that was interrupted leaves exactly this.

app.crash.rule.corrupted-archive.title.message: A file the game had to read is damaged or half-downloaded

app.crash.rule.datapack-blocked-world.fi.message: A mod that adds recipes or world generation was removed or changed. Put it back, or open the world with "safe mode" to load it without the broken datapack.

app.crash.rule.datapack-blocked-world.ti.message: The world would not load because a datapack has errors

app.crash.rule.disk-full.fix.message: Free some space on the drive the instance is on and launch again.

app.crash.rule.duplicate-mod-files.fix.message: Keep one of these and remove the rest: {files}

app.crash.rule.duplicate-mods.fix.message: Open the mods folder and leave one copy of each — two versions of the same file is the usual cause.

app.crash.rule.duplicate-mods.title.message: The same mod is installed more than once

app.crash.rule.exit-access-violation.fix.message: Most often the graphics driver or an overlay. Update the driver, turn shaders and overlays off, and launch again.

app.crash.rule.exit-access-violation.tit.message: Native code crashed the game without a report

app.crash.rule.exit-killed-by-system.fix.message: The computer ran out of memory as a whole. Give the game less, or close what else is running.

app.crash.rule.exit-killed-by-system.tit.message: The system ended the game to free memory

app.crash.rule.exit-missing-system-libra.message: Install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64), then let the launcher reinstall Java for this instance.
Java could not load a system library ({code})

app.crash.rule.exit-not-responding.fix.message: Large packs freeze for a while when a world loads, and clicking the window then makes Windows offer to close it. Leave it alone while it loads. If it froze for good, it was most likely short of memory.

app.crash.rule.exit-not-responding.title.message: Windows closed the game because it stopped responding

app.crash.rule.exit-stack-buffer-overrun.message: Usually an overlay or recorder hooking the game — MSI Afterburner, RivaTuner, OBS, the Discord overlay — or the graphics driver. Turn overlays off and update the driver.
Something hooked into the game crashed it

app.crash.rule.exit-stack-overflow.fix.message: Two mods calling each other endlessly, most of the time. Look at the mods changed since it last worked.

app.crash.rule.exit-stack-overflow.title.message: The game ran out of stack

app.crash.rule.fabric-wrong-dependency-v.message: Update {dependency} to {requirement}, or use a build of {mod_name} that fits.

app.crash.rule.feature-order-cycle.fix.message: Each is waiting for the other, so no order exists. Remove one of the world-generation mods, or install a mod that resolves the ordering.

app.crash.rule.feature-order-cycle.title.message: Two world-generation mods disagree about what comes first

app.crash.rule.ferritecore-neighbor-tabl.message: Set replaceNeighborLookup to false in config/ferritecore-mixin.toml until the mod named in the line below is fixed.
A mod clashed with FerriteCore’s memory savings

app.crash.rule.file-locked.fix.message: Close other launchers and any copy of the game still running, and check whether an antivirus is scanning this folder.

app.crash.rule.file-locked.title.message: Another program was holding one of the game’s files

app.crash.rule.gpu-driver.fix.message: Update the graphics driver from the maker’s site rather than through Windows Update, and turn off shaders while testing.

app.crash.rule.heap-too-large-to-start.f.message: Lower the allocation for this instance and launch again.

app.crash.rule.heap-too-large-to-start.t.message: The instance asked for more memory than could be reserved ({size})

app.crash.rule.install-incomplete.fix.message: The loader could not find Minecraft itself. Repair the instance so the launcher installs it again.

app.crash.rule.install-incomplete.title.message: The game or its loader is not fully installed

app.crash.rule.integrated-gpu-in-use.fix.message: If this computer also has a separate graphics card, the game is using the slower one. The launcher can ask Windows to use the other.

app.crash.rule.integrated-gpu-in-use.tit.message: The game is running on the built-in graphics chip ({renderer})

app.crash.rule.intel-cpu-instability.fix.message: Intel 13th and 14th generation desktop processors degrade and crash under load. Update the motherboard BIOS to one with Intel’s microcode fix; no change to mods helps if this is the cause.

app.crash.rule.intel-cpu-instability.tit.message: This processor ({model}) is known to become unstable

app.crash.rule.java-module-error.fix.message: Java refuses to start when two files claim the same module. The detail below names it — find which mods carry it and keep the newer one.

app.crash.rule.java-module-error.title.message: Two mods shipped the same library ({exception})

app.crash.rule.java-too-new.fix.message: Older versions of Minecraft need an older Java. Let the launcher install the one this version expects.

app.crash.rule.java-too-new.title.message: This Java is newer than the game can use

app.crash.rule.java-too-old.fix.message: Point this instance at a Java {needs} installation, or let it download one.

app.crash.rule.java-too-old.title.message: Something needs Java {needs}, and the instance ran on Java {has}

app.crash.rule.java-unsupported-class.fi.message: Change the Java this instance uses in its settings.

app.crash.rule.java-unsupported-class.ti.message: A mod was built for a newer Java than the one that ran

app.crash.rule.jna-blocked.fix.message: An antivirus, or a temporary folder without write permission, stops it. Add the launcher folder to the antivirus exclusions and check that the Windows TEMP folder is writable.

app.crash.rule.jna-blocked.title.message: A library could not unpack itself into the temporary folder

app.crash.rule.jvm-itself-failed.fix.message: A crash inside Java itself is either failing hardware or a bug in that Java build. Test the memory first; if it is clean, install a different Java version for this instance.

app.crash.rule.jvm-itself-failed.title.message: Java itself stopped, not the game

app.crash.rule.kubejs-datapack.fix.message: The file comes from a script in the kubejs folder. Fix or remove that script; a pack’s own scripts usually break after one of its mods is updated.

app.crash.rule.kubejs-datapack.title.message: A KubeJS script produced a broken datapack file ({file})

app.crash.rule.language-provider-mismatc.message: The lines below name what it wanted. Either update the loader for this instance, or take the build of that mod made for the loader you have.
A mod was built for a different version of the loader

app.crash.rule.loader-suggestion.title.message: The mod loader worked out a fix itself

app.crash.rule.missing-class-owner.fix.message: It expected {symbol}, which the installed {owner_name} does not have. An addon has to match the version of the mod it extends: update both, or roll {owner_name} back to what the addon was made for.

app.crash.rule.missing-class-owner.title.message: A mod was built for a different version of {owner_name}

app.crash.rule.missing-class.fix.message: It looked for {symbol} and no installed mod has it. Install the mod it depends on, or remove the one that needs it.

app.crash.rule.missing-class.title.message: A mod needs something that is not installed

app.crash.rule.missing-indium.fix.message: Sodium leaves out the rendering interface some mods draw through, and Indium puts it back. Install Indium for the same Minecraft version.

app.crash.rule.missing-indium.title.message: A mod needs Indium to draw with Sodium

app.crash.rule.missing-main-class.fix.message: The instance is incomplete — usually an install that was interrupted. Repair or reinstall it.

app.crash.rule.missing-main-class.title.message: The game could not be started at all ({class_name} is missing)

app.crash.rule.missing-native-library.fi.message: Repair the instance. If it happens again, check that an antivirus is not quarantining the natives folder.

app.crash.rule.missing-native-library.ti.message: A library the game loads from disk could not be loaded

app.crash.rule.mixin-failed.fix.message: The name in front of .mixins.json is the mod to update or remove first; when two mods patch the same thing, it is the pair that has to change.

app.crash.rule.mixin-failed.title.message: A mod could not patch the game ({config})

app.crash.rule.mixin-injection-failed.fi.message: Almost always the mod behind that file being built for a different version of the game or of another mod. Update it, and if it is already current, remove the mod it clashes with.

app.crash.rule.mixin-injection-failed.ti.message: A mod could not patch the game where it expected to ({config})

app.crash.rule.mixin-invalid-injection.f.message: Look at the mods named in the lines below and update them. If one of them is a performance or rendering mod, try without it first — those touch the most.

app.crash.rule.mixin-invalid-injection.t.message: Two mods changed the same part of the game

app.crash.rule.mod-for-other-version.fix.message: It went looking for {symbol}, which this version does not have. Update the mod, or use the version of it built for this one.

app.crash.rule.mod-for-other-version.tit.message: A mod was built for a different version of Minecraft

app.crash.rule.mod-incompatible.fix.message: The two cannot both be installed. Keep whichever you need and remove the other.

app.crash.rule.mods-changed-since-workin.message: Added: {added_count}, removed: {removed_count}. If nothing else here explains the crash, start with these — the list is in the lines below.
Mods changed since this instance last ran without crashing

app.crash.rule.native-allocator.fix.message: Almost always failing memory or a memory overclock. Run a RAM test, and turn off XMP or EXPO in the BIOS to see if it stops.

app.crash.rule.native-allocator.title.message: The memory allocator brought the process down ({library})

app.crash.rule.native-audio.fix.message: Usually the audio device changing while the game runs — headphones unplugged, a Bluetooth speaker going to sleep. Update the sound driver, and set a fixed output device.

app.crash.rule.native-audio.title.message: The sound system brought the process down

app.crash.rule.native-shader-macos.fix.message: A shader pack macOS cannot compile. Turn shaders off — most packs are written for drivers Apple does not ship.

app.crash.rule.native-shader-macos.title.message: The macOS graphics layer brought the process down

app.crash.rule.native-window-linux.fix.message: Update the graphics driver and Mesa. On Wayland, running the game through XWayland avoids most of these.

app.crash.rule.native-window-linux.title.message: A system graphics library brought the process down ({library})

app.crash.rule.neoforge-dependency-versi.message: Update {dependency} to a version in that range, or roll {mod_id} back to one that accepts what you have.

app.crash.rule.not-a-mod-file.fix.message: Usually a download that saved the web page instead of the file, or a resource pack put in the mods folder by mistake. Remove it and download it again.

app.crash.rule.oculus-without-embeddium..message: Oculus draws through Embeddium and cannot start without it. Install Embeddium, or on NeoForge use the official Sodium and Iris builds instead of either.

app.crash.rule.opengl-unsupported.fix.message: Update the graphics driver. On a laptop with two GPUs, make sure the game is set to run on the faster one.

app.crash.rule.opengl-unsupported.title.message: The graphics driver could not give the game the OpenGL it needs

app.crash.rule.optifine-present.fix.message: OptiFine breaks against most modern mods. Sodium with Iris, or Embeddium with Oculus, do the same job and are made to sit beside them.

app.crash.rule.optifine-present.title.message: OptiFine was loaded when this went wrong

app.crash.rule.out-of-memory-heap.fix.message: Give this instance more memory, or ask less of it: a lower render distance and fewer world-generation mods are what usually costs the most.

app.crash.rule.out-of-memory-heap.title.message: The game ran out of the memory it was given

app.crash.rule.out-of-memory-metaspace.f.message: This is a very large modpack on a small allocation. Raise the memory for this instance.

app.crash.rule.out-of-memory-metaspace.t.message: The game ran out of room for the code it was loading

app.crash.rule.out-of-memory-system.fix.message: Lower the memory this instance asks for, or close what else is running. Asking for more than the machine has is what stops it starting at all.

app.crash.rule.out-of-memory-system.titl.message: The machine had no memory left to give

app.crash.rule.resource-location-invalid.message: Minecraft only accepts lowercase Latin letters, digits and a few symbols in these names. The usual cause is the Windows account being named in another alphabet, which puts those letters in the path to everything. Move the launcher folder somewhere with a plain Latin path.
A name the game cannot use got into a path

app.crash.rule.server-config-broken.fix.message: It lives in that world’s serverconfig folder, not in config. Delete the file and open the world again — the mod writes a fresh one.

app.crash.rule.server-config-broken.titl.message: A world’s settings file is damaged ({file})

app.crash.rule.server-thread-stuck.fix.message: Something took so long that the game gave up waiting — usually world generation on a slow disk, or one mod stuck in a loop. The lines below name what it was doing.

app.crash.rule.server-thread-stuck.title.message: The world stopped responding and was shut down

app.crash.rule.software-renderer.fix.message: Windows is falling back to software rendering, which Minecraft cannot run on. Install the driver for your graphics card from its maker.

app.crash.rule.software-renderer.title.message: The game is drawing without a graphics driver ({renderer})

app.crash.rule.spark-profiler-crash.fix.message: Its native profiler does not work on newer Java. Update Spark, or run this instance on Java 21.

app.crash.rule.spark-profiler-crash.titl.message: Spark’s profiler brought the process down

app.crash.rule.suspect-mod.fix.message: Its own code was running when the game went down. Update it first; if that changes nothing, disable it and launch again to be sure.

app.crash.rule.suspected-mods.fix.message: Turn those off first, one at a time, and launch again after each.

app.crash.rule.too-many-block-ids.fix.message: Old versions of Minecraft have a hard limit here. Remove some content mods, or install one that raises the limit for that version.

app.crash.rule.too-many-block-ids.title.message: The pack ran out of ids for blocks or items

app.crash.rule.wrong-jdk-apple-silicon.f.message: An Apple Silicon Mac running an Intel Java, or the reverse. Let the launcher install Java for this instance rather than using one already on the system.

app.crash.rule.wrong-jdk-apple-silicon.t.message: Java is the wrong build for this Mac

instance.settings.tabs.java.modern-java-.message: This is new and not widely tested yet. Back up the instance before enabling it, and expect mods that assume Java 8 to misbehave.
Minecraft {gameVersion} normally only runs on Java 8. {provider} replaces LWJGL 2 and reworks Forge so the instance can run on a current Java release instead.
Disabling removes the launcher patches. Any mods it installed stay in the instance — remove them from the Mods tab if you no longer want them.
Picking a version downloads it and pins it as this instance’s Java installation. The lowest one is the best tested; newer ones are supported but less proven with mods for this Minecraft version.
